_comment: Media source manifest. tools/media.py reads this and writes processed assets into /media/. Sources live outside the repository in _source/ and are never deployed.

scene-graph-itc.alt: A 3D scene graph over the ITC building second floor. A single building node at the top connects down to a room node, then to a dense band of place nodes following the corridor loop, then to object nodes scattered along the walls, and finally to the reconstructed mesh of the floor.
scene-graph-itc.caption: The layered scene graph over the ITC second floor. It runs from one building node down through a room node, a band of place nodes following the corridor loop, and object nodes along the walls. Counts by category are in the legend.

perception-pipeline.alt: Pipeline diagram. Monocular RGB enters M2H-MX on the GPU, producing depth and semantics. Those feed pose-aware temporal alignment and a CPU-side VIO that uses predicted depth, with IMU input. The result is a metric semantic mesh and a 3D scene graph with building, room, place, object, and mesh layers.
perception-pipeline.caption: One camera and one IMU in, a layered scene graph out. Two arrows return from odometry into the perception block: the estimated pose is used to align the next dense prediction, not only to build the map.

mono-hydra-pp-pipeline.alt: Block diagram of the Mono-Hydra++ system showing perception, odometry, and mapping stages and the data passing between them.
mono-hydra-pp-pipeline.caption: Where each learned output enters the estimator.

scannet-radius.alt: Three floor plans side by side for ScanNet scene 0054. The first shows ground truth object centres as coloured dots, the second shows predicted object centres as squares, the third overlays them showing matched, missing, and unmatched objects.
scannet-radius.caption: Object placement on ScanNet scene 0054, scored by radius match at 0.5 m. Green is matched, orange is a ground-truth object the system missed, and a red cross is something predicted that is not there. The aggregate figure for this metric is 42.59 percent.

scannet-failure.alt: Semantic mesh reconstruction compared against ground truth, showing small object classes absorbed into larger neighbouring surfaces.
scannet-failure.caption: A failure case. Small classes are absorbed into the dominant surface next to them, which the global mIoU of 44.96 percent does not show on its own.

uhumans2-loop.alt: Three trajectory plots on the uHumans2 dataset comparing ground truth against a baseline and against the system with depth sparse factors and a semantic mask, marking accepted, available, and missed loop closure candidates.
uhumans2-loop.caption: Loop closure behaviour on uHumans2. Of 233 candidates the baseline finds 212 and misses 21; adding depth sparse factors and the semantic mask shifts which candidates survive rather than simply finding more.

uhumans2-ablation.alt: Overview of the uHumans2 component ablation, showing trajectory and mapping quality across configurations.
uhumans2-ablation.caption: The component study. Different configurations give the best result on different metrics.

m2h-mx-architecture.alt: M2H-MX architecture diagram. A DINOv3 backbone with LoRA adaptation feeds token reassembly and a feature pyramid, then register-gated Mamba blocks at each scale, task adaptors, a cross-task mixer, multi-scale convolutional attention, and finally the task heads.
m2h-mx-architecture.caption: M2H-MX. The backbone stays mostly frozen and LoRA adapts the later blocks, so the compute goes into the decoder and the cross-task exchange rather than into retraining the features.

m2h-mx-rgm.alt: The register-gated Mamba block. A global register vector passes through a linear layer and sigmoid to produce a channel-wise gate that modulates reshaped feature tokens before a Mamba block.
m2h-mx-rgm.caption: The register-gated Mamba block. One global vector gates every decoder scale, so global scene layout reaches local decoding without the cost of full attention.

m2h-mx-ctm-msca.alt: Cross-task mixer followed by multi-scale convolutional attention, showing how auxiliary task features modulate a target task before spatial refinement.
m2h-mx-ctm-msca.caption: Cross-task mixing, then spatial refinement. Removing both costs 2.07 mIoU; replacing the backbone costs 8.81.

scenegraph-system-design.alt: System design diagram for monocular 3D scene graph construction, showing the perception networks, visual-inertial odometry, and the scene graph layers.
scenegraph-system-design.caption: The original Mono-Hydra design: two independent networks for depth and semantics, feeding a robocentric VIO and the Hydra scene graph layers.

itc-embedded.alt: Reconstruction of the ITC second floor produced from the embedded operating point on the Jetson Orin NX at reduced input resolution.
itc-embedded.caption: The same floor rebuilt from the Jetson operating point at 256x192. Mean error is 0.22 m here against 0.08 m at full resolution.

portrait.alt: Bavantha Udugama, in a dark suit and tie against a plain warm grey background.

drone-side.alt: The custom quadrotor on a wooden table, seen from the side. A carbon fibre frame with a protective cage around four red propellers, the flight controller and wiring visible on top, and the compute board mounted underneath.
drone-side.caption: Carbon fibre frame, caged propellers, and the Jetson Orin NX underneath that runs perception, odometry, mapping, and scene graph construction.

drone-top.alt: The same quadrotor from directly above, showing the square carbon frame, four red propellers inside their cage, the orange lithium battery strapped across the centre, and a cooling fan on the compute board.
drone-top.caption: From above: battery across the centre, compute and its cooling fan beneath.

drone-angle.alt: The quadrotor from a three-quarter angle, showing the depth of the carbon frame, the propeller cage, and the battery and electronics stacked in the centre.
drone-angle.caption: Three-quarter view.

wipe-rgb.label: RGB input

mx-indoor-depth.label: Predicted depth

mx-indoor-semantics.alt: Predicted semantic labels for the same living room, with flat colour regions for sofa, chair, lamp, table, floor, wall, and pictures.

mx-outdoor-rgb.alt: A city street seen from a vehicle: parked and moving cars, a yellow DHL lorry, road markings, traffic signs, trees, and buildings.

mx-outdoor-depth.label: Predicted depth

itc-loop.alt: Screen recording of the scene graph being built while the drone flies the ITC second floor loop. The graph grows from nothing to a full corridor circuit, with live RGB, semantic, and depth views alongside.
itc-loop.caption: The scene graph forming over one loop of the ITC second floor, from the first frame to loop closure. Playback is 10x real time. Live RGB, predicted semantics, and predicted depth run down the right.

icra26.alt: Screen recording of ScanNet scene 0000. A hierarchical 3D scene graph hangs from a building node down through room and place nodes to labelled object boxes over the reconstructed mesh, while the RGB frame, the predicted semantics, and the predicted depth run down the right.
icra26.caption: The whole pipeline on ScanNet scene 0000. M2H-MX predicts depth and semantics from the image stream, Mono-Hydra++ consumes those predictions inside the visual-inertial odometry and the mapping backend, and the hierarchical scene graph is built in real time. Playback is 16x.

scope-explorer.alt: Simulated indoor exploration run showing the robot's occupancy map growing as it selects routes through the environment.
scope-explorer.caption: Autonomous exploration in simulation. The robot holds an occupancy map it has built itself and commits to one certified route at a time, so the map fills in region by region rather than by wandering. 60 second excerpt.

stairs-zupt.alt: Screen recording on the drone's Jetson. An rviz window shows predicted depth, tracked features, and predicted semantics down the left, and the estimated trajectory climbing a stairwell in the centre, labelled MOVING while the drone is in motion and ZUPT STATIONARY while it is still.
stairs-zupt.caption: Depth-backed visual-inertial odometry on the drone's Jetson, walked down and back up the stairs at home. The label switches between MOVING and ZUPT STATIONARY: when the platform is still, zero-velocity updates hold the estimate in place instead of letting it drift. Predicted depth, tracked features, and predicted semantics are the panels on the left.

drone-flight.alt: The custom quadrotor lifting off from the floor of an indoor walkway and flying down it towards the camera, past timber and glass balconies.
drone-flight.caption: Take-off and a pass down the corridor. Everything the mapping runs on is carried onboard.

humanoid-deployment.alt: Two branded humanoid service robots driving themselves across the floor of a busy exhibition stand, moving among standing visitors and around furniture.
humanoid-deployment.caption: Service humanoids running autonomously at a client event in Dubai, navigating a floor full of people and furniture. Deployment work at Expert Hub Robotics, where I built the navigation stack and led the on-site rollout.

humanoid-mapping.alt: A laptop beside one of the humanoid robots, showing a 2D occupancy grid of the venue being filled in as the robot drives, with the robot's pose marked in red.
humanoid-mapping.caption: The map behind it. A 2D occupancy grid of the venue built with GMapping-based SLAM while the robot drives, with its estimated pose in red. This is what the navigation stack plans over.

m2h-mx-indoor.title: Indoor, NYUDv2
m2h-mx-indoor.caption: One indoor frame, three ways. M2H-MX predicts metric depth and semantic labels from the single RGB image on the left. The mapping backend consumes these two outputs.
m2h-mx-indoor.captionShort: Indoor frame, NYUDv2. Metric depth and semantic labels from one RGB image.

m2h-mx-outdoor.title: Outdoor, Cityscapes
m2h-mx-outdoor.caption: The same model on a street scene. M2H-MX is built for indoor mapping and still reaches 82.28 mIoU on Cityscapes, 3.15 points above the strongest baseline compared.
m2h-mx-outdoor.captionShort: The same model outdoors, Cityscapes: 82.28 mIoU, 3.15 points over the strongest baseline.

itc-corridor.title: ITC building corridor
itc-corridor.caption: One frame from the ITC corridor sequence, shown as the camera image, the predicted depth, and the predicted semantic labels.
itc-corridor.captionShort: One frame from the ITC corridor sequence: camera image, predicted depth, predicted labels.
